rows.capability: The complete editor shell presents the established header, layer controls, preview, timeline, and secondary tools as one coherent workspace.
Typography, density, colors, controls, spacing, and feedback retain the recognizable editor visual language.
Resizable editor regions remain smooth, bounded, and persistent during active editing.
Established keyboard shortcuts work in the right contexts without stealing text-entry input.
Users can add, remove, duplicate, and reorder visualization layers.
Users can efficiently discover visualization types, add them, and keep a clear active-layer selection.
Layer visibility, opacity, blend mode, freeze, debug, and related compositing controls remain available.
Layer cards preserve clear identity, selection, expansion, compact controls, and contextual actions.
Component schemas generate complete, usable parameter editors.
Layer presets and reset behavior remain available and predictable.
Dragging and typing parameter values updates the preview quickly and smoothly.
Stage presents production-quality model-backed DJ and crowd characters with authored dance animation across its established cinematic camera paths.
The full node-graph editor opens from layer workflows and preserves the established spatial editing experience.
Users can search for, create, select, move, and delete all supported node types.
Connections provide clear type compatibility, feedback, replacement, and invalid-edge handling.
Graph presets and copy/paste workflows retain their productive V1 behavior.
Node graphs evaluate continuously from transport, audio, and parameter inputs and drive visible layer values.
Users can load supported local audio files and receive clear progress or error feedback.
Waveform display, zoom, scroll, playhead, and seek interactions remain precise and smooth.
Bundled audio choices and track navigation remain usable from the editor.
Live or captured audio input remains available with explicit permission, lifecycle, and failure handling.
Volume and mute-like behavior remain immediate, accessible, and synchronized with the active audio engine.
Play, pause, seek, restart, and loop controls retain precise V1 behavior.
The timeline communicates duration and playhead state and supports direct navigation.
The editor preview continuously renders the canonical scene through the V2 runtime contract.
Multiple layers composite in order with their intended visibility, opacity, and blend semantics.
Layer-level preview or mirror tooling remains available for focused editing.
Undo and redo cover meaningful editor operations with correct grouping and deterministic restoration.
The UI communicates whether history applies to layer, graph, or broader project context.
Projects save, load, and reset through the canonical V2 document contract.
Users can drag or select a project document for import with clear validation feedback.
Bundled sample projects remain discoverable and valid canonical examples.
Users can export a still image from the intended scene, frame, size, and background settings.
Video export retains configuration, progress, cancellation, and deterministic scene rendering.
Debug overlays and layer diagnostics remain accessible without contaminating normal output.
The profiler exposes useful render and component timing for diagnosing scene performance.
Live performance statistics remain available and accurate enough for editor feedback.
Rhythm Lab remains a complete secondary workspace with its established panels and navigation.
Grid, onset, and related rhythm-analysis controls produce understandable and repeatable feedback.
Representative V1 scenes play smoothly in the V2 editor at comparable or better responsiveness.
Layer, parameter, node, panel, and transport interactions remain immediately responsive under representative project load.
Extended editing, playback, track switching, and panel use do not accumulate resources or degrade responsiveness.
